title: Kuku Technologies IPO: What SEBI's Nod Means for Investors
description: Kuku Technologies has received approval from SEBI to launch its Initial Public Offering (IPO). The company previously filed its confidential draft IPO papers .

faq.a: An Initial Public Offering (IPO) is the process by which a private company offers shares of its stock to the public for the first time. It allows the company to raise capital from public investors and get listed on a stock exchange.

faq.q: What is SEBI's role in an IPO?
faq.a: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) is the market regulator that approves IPOs. It reviews the company's Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) to ensure full disclosure, transparency, and compliance with regulations, protecting investor interests.

faq.q: How can I apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) facility via net banking or through your stockbroker's platform. You will need an active Demat and trading account.

faq.q: What is a lot size in an IPO?
faq.a: A lot size is the minimum number of shares an investor must apply for in an IPO. You cannot apply for a single share; you must bid for shares in multiples of the specified lot size.

faq.q: Are IPOs guaranteed to give listing gains?
faq.a: No, IPOs are not guaranteed to give listing gains. While some IPOs may list at a premium, others can list at a discount or trade flat. Market conditions, company fundamentals, and investor sentiment all play a role in listing performance.

faq.q: How are IPO gains taxed in India?
faq.a: Gains from selling IPO shares are taxed as Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) if held for less than 12 months (taxed at 15% if STT paid) or Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) if held for more than 12 months (exempt up to ₹1 lakh, then 10% if STT paid).
